service.description: NOTE: this service is meant for internal use and authentication is not required. Do not export or allow this service to be called remotely.

Send a stored EmailMessage that is not a draft. The server is the message's emailServerId, else the EmailServer of its mail client account (emailAccountId). A message of the mail client also brings its identity's reply-to address, its EmailMessageAttachment files (inline ones by Content-ID, in a related part) and its In-Reply-To and References headers (inReplyTo, referencesHeader). A Ready or Bounced message becomes Sent with its new messageId. A delivery that fails is a message, not an error, as in Java, and its text is sendError. A client message (one with an emailAccountId) is the mail client's to keep: what stops it after the status checks is its sendError, not an error, and its Sent status is written in the caller's transaction (a template's message in a new one, as in Java). An SMTP session that does not end within two minutes is a sendError with an uncertain deliveryOutcome.

parameter.name: markSent
parameter.description: False leaves a client message's status as it is: the mail client's deliver#DraftMessage records the result in a transaction of its own (record#SendResult)

parameter.name: messageId
parameter.description: The Message-ID it went out with; empty when nothing was sent

parameter.name: deliveryOutcome
parameter.description: On an SMTP failure, as send#EmailTemplate's: retryable for an explicit temporary rejection or a server that was not reached, permanent for an explicit permanent rejection, uncertain when acceptance is unknown.

service.description: Whether a server's settings work, for the mail account wizard; nothing is changed. SMTP connects, upgrades to TLS as configured and signs in; the store (when it has a storeHost) connects and signs in, and IMAP lists its folders. Each step is {step (smtp, storeLogin, storeList), ok, message}. folderList has each IMAP folder's {folderPath, delimiter, attributeList, folderKindEnumId}: INBOX, else its special-use attribute (\Sent, \Drafts, \Trash, \Junk, \Archive), else EfkOther. Use org.moqui.mail.EmailClientServices.test#EmailAccount, which checks the user may manage the account. SMTP signs in as smtpUsername when the server has one, else as mailUsername; smtpUsername and smtpPassword given here are tried instead of the stored ones (nothing is stored), so a wizard can test a separate SMTP sign-in before saving it.

parameter.name: smtpUsername
parameter.description: Given (even empty: the store's sign-in), the SMTP user to try

parameter.name: smtpPassword
parameter.description: Given, the SMTP password to try

service.description: What the handler of a mail queue kind gets (moqui_core::edge::queue::apply): the item, on the node that received it, run as _EDGE_ in the transaction of its receipt. contentLocation is where this node kept the item's content (the message), removed once the delivery is answered. An error the handler adds rolls the receipt back, so the sender tries the item again, counted; retryLater (the reason) rolls it back too, for a cause that is not the item's (a relay or database away), and the item waits, not counted.

parameter.name: pairedNodeId
parameter.description: The local node of the pair (on a local node, its own id)

service.description: On a local node, the queue kind mail: a message the edge node's listener took (the payload has its envelope and recipient addresses with their DSN parameters, the content is the message), delivered as the SMTP listener delivers to the hosted and shared accounts the addresses resolve to here; the edge node's account ids are never used. An address no account takes now is logged and left out. A store that fails answers retryLater, so the queue tries again, not counted; an account that stored it has its Message-ID and does not store it twice. A message that is not mail is an error. Refused on an edge node.

On an edge node, the queue kind mailOut: a message its local node sent through an EmailServer with smtpHost edge:, sent from the VERP sender bounce+(item id)@(edge_mail_bounce_domain) when that is set. With edge_mail_mta moqui (the default) it is DKIM-signed and recorded as one moqui.edge.EdgeMailDelivery per recipient domain in this item's transaction, which the MX delivery thread delivers (moqui_mail::mx); the answers come back as mailStatus from there. With edge_mail_mta postfix it is relayed to the MTA beside the edge node (edge_mail_relay_host, edge_mail_relay_port), and its answer (accepted, or bounced for a 5xx or an address it could never take, with the reply) queued back as mailStatus in a transaction of its own; an item whose answer is queued is not relayed again. A relay that cannot be reached, answers 4xx or drops the connection answers retryLater. Refused on a local node.

On a local node, the queue kind mailStatus: the edge node's answer (from its relay, or a later delivery status notification to the VERP address) for one of this node's mailOut items, which names the message; nothing the edge node names is trusted for it. A bounce puts a mail client's message back in the Outbox (ES_READY with sendError, no folder) and marks another message ES_BOUNCED with sendError, only while it is still Sent with the Message-ID it went out with; accepted and delayed are logged. Refused on an edge node.

On a local node, the failed-service of the queue kind mailOut: a message that never reached the edge node (unpaired, past the retention period or the size cap) is put back as a bounce is, with the reason as its sendError, so the failure is not silent.

The DNS TXT record of this node's DKIM key (mail_dkim_key, generated into runtime/.env the first time it is needed), to publish at (selector)._domainkey.(domain): v=DKIM1; k=rsa; p=(public key). The domains are mail_dkim_domains, else the domains of the hosted and shared accounts.

Poll an email server (IMAP or POP3) to receive messages. Each new message is processed using the Email-ECA rules. Messages are flagged as seen (if supported). Messages are deleted if the storeDelete flag is set on the moqui.basic.email.EmailServer record.
This is meant to be called as a scheduled service, run as often as you want to poll for new messages on a particular server (configured in the corresponding moqui.basic.email.EmailServer record).
Add a job in the quartz_data.xml file for this service to run this scheduled.

return.message: Found duplicate message with Message-ID [${messageId}] from server [${emailServerId}]

service-call.name: create#moqui.basic.email.EmailMessage
service-call.in-map: {sentDate:fields.sentDate, receivedDate:fields.receivedDate, statusId:statusId, subject:fields.subject, body:body, fromAddress:fields.from, toAddresses:fields.toList?.join(', '), ccAddresses:fields.ccList?.join(', '), bccAddresses:fields.bccList?.join(', '), messageId:messageId, emailServerId:emailServerId}

parameter.name: toAddresses
parameter.description: Comma separated list of to email addresses

parameter.name: ccAddresses
parameter.description: Comma separated list of CC email addresses

parameter.name: bccAddresses
parameter.description: Comma separated list of BCC email addresses
